publications.title: Interpreting Latent CoT Reasoning as Dynamical Systems
publications.venueFull: ICML 2026 Workshop on Foundations of Deep Generative Models: Understanding Memorization, Generalization, and Reasoning
publications.role: Co-first author and lead pipeline engineer (Algoverse AI Research Fellowship)
publications.tldr: Latent chain-of-thought trajectories form structured dynamical systems: CODI behaves as a stable attractor, COCONUT as an unstable expanding system, and Sim-CoT supervision tightens both without changing the underlying dynamics.
publications.abstract: Recent latent reasoning methods such as CODI and COCONUT face a fundamental interpretability problem: they carry multiple superimposed candidate traces in hidden space at each step, which obscures how reasoning evolves. We model the sequence of latent tokens as a trajectory in representation space and apply dynamical-systems analysis to characterize reasoning evolution. Using quantitative metrics (step-to-step change, direction consistency, Lyapunov sensitivity) and qualitative projections (UMAP, DMD, PHATE), we show that latent CoT exhibits structured, non-random dynamics with two distinct stability classes.
findings: CODI behaves as a stable attractor: latent states converge into a bounded region, and shorter, simpler paths correlate with correct answers.
COCONUT behaves as an unstable expanding system: latent states spread outward across steps, and more latent work correlates with correctness.
Sim-CoT supervision tightens both behaviours without changing the underlying dynamics.

COCONUT shows three-attractor compression with a mid-chain direction-consistency hinge at step 3, while CODI behaves as a near period-2 oscillator with 85% of samples carrying at least one unstable DMD mode (41% for COCONUT). Signatures hold across GSM8K and MATH.
stats: 22 quantitative plots per run and 28 of 28 reproducible numeric claims verified

figures.caption: CODI trajectories projected onto dominant DMD modes contract toward a bounded region.

publications.title: Toward Fairness-Aware Human Feedback for Table Unionability
publications.role: Co-first author, research assistant under Dr. Roee Shraga (BSF Grant 2024022)
publications.tldr: First adaptation of the FairEM framework from entity matching to annotator-level fairness in table union search, showing that human feedback should be treated as conditionally reliable.
publications.abstract: Table union search is a foundational primitive in modern data lakes, and human feedback is increasingly used to supervise it. We adapt the FairEM framework (Shahbazi et al., VLDB 2023) from entity matching to annotator-level fairness and ask whether feedback quality varies systematically across demographic groups. On a 480-row dataset of 60 annotators across 8 questions and 4 survey versions, we find statistically significant disparities that survive multiple-testing correction and five orthogonal cleaning strategies.
findings: 6 of 10 FairEM metrics flag unfairness against non-native English annotators.
25% versus 44% accuracy on hard questions (Fisher exact p = 0.031).
The non-native, lower-education, young triple intersection persists at p_BH = 0.037 after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction.
Robust across 5 of 5 orthogonal data-cleaning strategies; behavioral disparities exceed demographic ones.
stats: 480-row dataset: 60 annotators x 8 questions x 4 survey versions
10,000-shuffle permutation tests and 10,000-resample stratified bootstrap CIs

research.title: Latent chain-of-thought trajectories as dynamical systems
research.role: AI Research Fellow, lead pipeline engineer
research.summary: Selected for the competitive 12-week Algoverse fellowship; modeled latent chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs as discrete-time dynamical systems and reproduced two latent-reasoning training methods end to end on GPT-2.
highlights: Applied Dynamic Mode Decomposition, PHATE, UMAP, t-SNE and PCA to 768-dimensional latent trajectories across 8,792 GSM8K and 500 MATH samples, producing 22 quantitative plots per run.

Reproduced CODI self-distillation (parallel teacher-student with a 3-loss objective) and the COCONUT 4-stage latent curriculum as LoRA adapters (rank 128, alpha 32) on stock GPT-2 with PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers and PEFT; recovered 99.84% of test samples with a positional overflow guard.

Engineered the reliability layer: a multi-stage Bash and Python orchestrator with CUDA health polling that stabilized 14+ hour training runs, HDF5 resume-from-cache saving about 90 minutes per recovery, a GPU-resident Kraskov KSG-1 mutual-information estimator, and a safetensors-level checkpoint repair that preserved trained embeddings byte for byte.
Built a verification harness that passes 28 of 28 reproducible numeric claims on the canonical run.

research.title: FairPrep: demographic fairness for table union search
research.summary: First adaptation of the FairEM framework to annotator-level fairness in table union search, with a complete statistical methodology stack.
highlights: Built 9 source modules across 5 experimental phases on a 480-row dataset (60 annotators x 8 questions x 4 survey versions).

Designed the statistical stack: 10 FairEM confusion-matrix metrics, permutation testing (10,000 shuffles), bootstrap confidence intervals (10,000 stratified resamples), Fisher exact tests, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, and dual-track logistic regression (scikit-learn for interpretation, statsmodels for inference).
Surfaced statistically significant bias against non-native English annotators on hard questions (25% versus 44% accuracy, p = 0.031), robust across 5 of 5 cleaning strategies.

projects.name: Interpreting Latent CoT Reasoning as Dynamical Systems
projects.subtitle: Mechanistic interpretability paper, ICML 2026 FoGen Workshop poster
projects.summary: Treats each latent thought token of a chain-of-thought language model as a state in a discrete-time trajectory and applies dynamical-systems analysis to 768-dimensional reasoning trajectories across 8,792 GSM8K and 500 MATH samples.
projects.problem: Latent reasoning methods such as CODI and COCONUT keep multiple superimposed candidate traces in hidden space at every step, so existing mechanistic tools reveal compression and shortcuts but cannot explain how reasoning evolves from one latent step to the next.
projects.approach: Model the six latent hidden states as a trajectory; measure step-to-step change, direction consistency, arc length, a Lyapunov surrogate and perturbation divergence; project with DMD, PHATE, UMAP, PCA and t-SNE across four model configurations (CODI and COCONUT, vanilla and Sim-CoT) on GPT-2-small.
highlights: CODI behaves as a stable attractor while COCONUT behaves as an unstable expanding system; Sim-CoT supervision tightens both without changing the dynamics.
Reproduced CODI self-distillation and the COCONUT four-stage latent curriculum end to end as rank-128 LoRA adapters with PyTorch, Transformers and PEFT.

Built the reliability layer: CUDA health-polling orchestration for 14+ hour runs, HDF5 resume-from-cache, a GPU-resident Kraskov KSG-1 mutual-information estimator and a byte-exact safetensors checkpoint repair.
Verification harness passes 28 of 28 reproducible numeric claims; fixed seeds, greedy decoding and pinned dependencies throughout.

projects.name: Einstein Vision: 3D scene reconstruction for autonomous driving
projects.subtitle: Perception stack plus TensorRT inference optimization
projects.summary: Converts monocular dash-cam video into scene-accurate 3D reconstructions by fusing depth, detection, segmentation, pose and optical-flow models, then renders the scene with the Blender Python API while streaming masks and poses at 30 FPS.
projects.problem: Dash-cam footage lacks interpretable 3D context for perception debugging and for explaining autonomous-driving decisions to humans.
projects.approach: Fused MiDaS and Depth Anything monocular depth, Detic open-vocabulary detection with a custom vocabulary, YOLO3D vehicle yaw and boxes, OpenPifPaf and OSX body keypoints, Mask R-CNN lanes and road markings, and RAFT optical flow; calibrated a pinhole camera model and projected detections into world coordinates; synthesized LiDAR-like point clouds and lane contours as ground truth. Rendered through Blender EEVEE with typed asset collections, per-sequence transforms and deterministic replays for side-by-side comparison; input was 13 Tesla Model S dash-cam sequences.
highlights: Improved 3D placement accuracy 50% and scene realism 75% across 13 driving sequences.
Deployed detectors through TorchScript to ONNX to TensorRT FP16 with layer fusion: 1.5x multi-object throughput and 35% lower p95 latency, validated with NVIDIA Nsight.
Documented failure modes honestly: tunnel reflections, rain on the lens, class flicker between SUV and pickup, and optical-flow direction errors at low speed.

projects.name: Where does physics live in vision encoders?
projects.subtitle: Spatial probing and LoRA ablation of VLM physical reasoning

projects.name: AutoGit-AI: VS Code extension with secret scanning
projects.subtitle: Shipped on the VS Code Marketplace
projects.summary: Save a file and AutoGit stages it, writes an AI commit message with GitHub Copilot, scans the diff for leaked secrets and pushes. The only auto-commit extension with a built-in secret scanner that blocks keys, tokens and passwords before they reach the remote.
projects.problem: Auto-commit removes the human review step between saving and pushing, which is exactly when secrets leak; AI-assisted commits leak at roughly twice the baseline rate.
projects.approach: Pattern plus entropy scanning of only the added lines (AWS, GitHub, GitLab, Google, Slack, Stripe, npm, SendGrid, OpenAI and Anthropic keys, JWTs, private-key blocks, connection strings); fails closed on oversized diffs; fingerprint-bound overrides; gitignore-style excludes enforced at staging time; skips merges, rebases and detached HEAD; git invoked with argument arrays, never shell strings.
highlights: Published on the VS Code Marketplace as ShreyaBoyane.auto-git-copilot under Apache-2.0, with CI that lints, tests and packages on every push.
Pure logic lives in a fully unit-tested library; VS Code wiring is isolated in the extension entry point.
Debounced batching, protected branches, status-bar control and a full output-channel log.

projects.summary: A self-attentive sequential recommender with multi-head attention, causal masking and residual feed-forward blocks for next-item ranking, tuned with hyperparameter sweeps and selected by offline metrics.
projects.problem: Sparse interaction histories make next-item prediction unstable; the goal was a compact model that holds up under sparsity.
projects.approach: Swept dropout 0.05 to 0.5, attention heads 1 to 2 and hidden dimensions 5 to 50, visualized stability across five variants and picked the best checkpoint by nDCG and hit rate.
highlights: nDCG@10 of 0.3166 and Hit@10 of 0.4913 at epoch 14 with a two-block, 50-dimensional configuration.

projects.name: Eigenfaces and latent face generation
projects.subtitle: Probabilistic PCA versus beta-VAE
projects.summary: Trained probabilistic PCA and beta-VAE models on 576-dimensional face vectors for unsupervised identity representation and generation, then compared reconstructions and latent interpolations.
projects.problem: How much of a face survives a 16-, 32- or 64-dimensional latent, and which model interpolates more smoothly.
projects.approach: Reduced to latent spaces of 16, 32 and 64 dimensions with 95%+ variance retained, generated 100 novel faces by decoder sampling, and compared models through PCA-projected visualizations and 10x10 output grids.
highlights: VAE showed stronger feature continuity and expressiveness; decoder sampling cut training time 35% over dense baselines.

projects.name: Behavioral cloning in Atari Pong
projects.subtitle: Imitation learning with a 3-layer CNN
projects.summary: A supervised imitation-learning pipeline that clones an expert Pong policy from Arcade Learning Environment demonstrations with a three-layer convolutional network.
projects.problem: Can a small CNN reproduce expert paddle control from demonstrations alone without reward signals.
projects.approach: Trained on expert frames for 100 epochs, validated through loss trajectories and gameplay video logs, and measured action latency.
highlights: 87.55% test accuracy with minimal overfitting; the cloned agent tracks the paddle with sub-500 ms action latency.

projects.name: Map.AR: augmented reality navigation assistant
projects.subtitle: Indoor and outdoor AR wayfinding, TECHVED sponsored
projects.summary: An augmented-reality navigation assistant that guides users to a destination indoors and outdoors, combining Vuforia marker detection with Unity 3D overlays and place recommendations based on user preferences.
projects.problem: Complex indoor spaces are hard to navigate with 2D maps.
projects.approach: Built the indoor navigation feature, the recommendation logic and the entire frontend in Unity and C# with Vuforia, Autodesk Revit models, Maps SDK and Firebase; designed the UI in Figma.
highlights: Piloted with college users at 90%+ satisfaction on a usability survey; robust across lighting conditions.
Secured industry sponsorship from TECHVED in October 2021 and presented a seminar on AR development tools.

projects.name: Real-time sign language detection
projects.subtitle: Custom SSD object detector
projects.summary: An end-to-end custom object-detection system that recognizes hand gestures and translates sign language into text in real time for people with hearing impairments.
projects.problem: Communication barriers for users of sign language in everyday settings.
projects.approach: Trained a Single Shot Multibox Detector in TensorFlow on a custom gesture dataset and integrated it with a live camera feed.
highlights: Accurate real-time detection and translation of multiple gestures.

projects.name: Real-time face mask detection
projects.subtitle: MobileNet SSD on live video
projects.summary: A lightweight MobileNet SSD detector that checks whether people are wearing face masks on live video feeds, built for COVID-19 compliance monitoring in public spaces.
projects.problem: Institutions needed an automated, low-cost way to monitor mask compliance.
projects.approach: Trained a custom MobileNet SSD model and integrated it with video streams for real-time inference.
highlights: Deployed for live detection with high accuracy, suitable for institutions and public venues.

projects.name: BookADDA: peer-to-peer book rental platform
projects.subtitle: Full-stack web app for students
projects.summary: An online platform where students buy, rent or sell books with fellow students, with a search-first interface and a Flask backend.
projects.problem: Textbooks are expensive and campus book exchange was informal and slow.
projects.approach: Designed and implemented the entire frontend in HTML, CSS, Bootstrap and JavaScript and integrated it with a Python Flask and MySQL backend.
highlights: Launched a working platform that received positive feedback for ease of use and search.

projects.name: shreyaboyane.dev: this site
projects.subtitle: Content-graph-driven portfolio with a depth-map hero
projects.summary: A Next.js 16 and React 19 site driven by one JSON content graph that feeds every page, the JSON-LD, the sitemap, llms.txt and an HTML resume, with a WebGL2 hero that renders a depth map of the portrait produced by Depth Anything V2.
projects.problem: The previous version drifted a full degree-completion behind reality because content was hardcoded in four places, and its particle background read as a template.
projects.approach: Single source of truth in content/profile.json with a build-time drift guard; Tailwind 4 OKLCH tokens; Motion-Primitives for interactive islands; raw WebGL2 point cloud displaced by depth; static generation for all routes; markdown content negotiation and llms.txt for AI agents; pitch videos rendered with Hyperframes.
highlights: Every route is static; no runtime API.
One h1 per page, Person and ProfilePage JSON-LD with full sameAs, VideoObject schema per pitch video.
